rec-20261118-5011.point: The movants ask for a 30-day extension of the comment period on MISO's November 16 filing.
rec-20261118-5011.quote: move for a 30-day extension of time to submit comments on Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.’s (“MISO”) November 16, 2026 filing

rec-20261118-5011.point: First reason: Congress is debating a bill that could bear on MISO's filing.
rec-20261118-5011.quote: Congress is actively debating the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (“BAAJA”)

rec-20261118-5011.point: They say a section of the bill on transmission cost allocation may conflict with MISO's filing.
rec-20261118-5011.quote: BAAJA Section 2107 contains directives regarding transmission cost allocation that may be inconsistent with MISO’s filing

rec-20261118-5011.point: Second reason: the ordinary comment period is too short for this proceeding.
rec-20261118-5011.quote: the ordinary comment period is insufficient to allow parties to address the many issues raised by this complex and lengthy proceeding

rec-20261118-5011.point: They say MISO has split its response across at least four other section 205 filings.
rec-20261118-5011.quote: MISO has filed at least four piecemeal 205 filings prior to, or simultaneous with, the instant matter

rec-20261118-5011.point: They ask for a comment date on the motion and a ruling within a week.
rec-20261118-5011.quote: request the Commission set a comment date of November 19, 2026, on this motion, and render a decision by November 23, 2026

rec-20261118-5011.point: The requested new deadline is January 15, 2027.
rec-20261118-5011.quote: GRANTING the requested extension of time, until January 15, 2027, to comment on MISO’s filing

filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.point: A new Large Load Project Review would study every large-load service request, with deposits and milestones to deter speculative ones.
filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.quote: The LLPR also includes deposits, project milestones, and other safeguards designed to discourage speculative Large Load requests.

filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.point: Large-load customers would bear the cost of the upgrades built for them through cost recovery agreements.
filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.quote: designed to ensure that the costs incurred to provide Transmission Service to Large Load Transmission Customers, including the costs of Large Load Upgrades (defined herein), are born by such customers

filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.point: MISO would publish the location and estimated costs of large loads on a dashboard.
filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.quote: The results of the LLPR periodically will be published to provide transparency into the location and estimated costs associated with Large Load facilities in the MISO region

filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.point: Two new services, Firm Service Step Up and Interim NITS, would let customers take service in stages as they build out.
filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.quote: The new Transmission Services available to Large Loads include Firm Service Step Up and Interim Non-Firm NITS service.

filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.point: Loads of 200 MW or more partnered with a generator for at least 15 years go through the resource study instead.
filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.quote: If the Large Load is greater than or equal to 200 MW and has formally partnered with a generator for a minimum of fifteen years, then the applicants will go through the LARS study process.

filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.point: Transmission owners' study reports filed with a large-load application must say which alternative transmission technologies were considered and what was decided.
filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.quote: requires Large Load Transmission Customers to include with their LLLPR Application the applicable Transmission Owner’s Interconnection Study Report, specifically identifying what ATTs and GETs were considered

filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.point: The application also carries the owner's cost estimate, which MISO says gives the cost transparency the order sought.
filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.quote: This information will enable MISO to verify any analyses performed by the Transmission Owner and provide the cost transparency sought by the Show Cause Order.

filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.point: A load that wants to co-locate with generation must first have an interconnection agreement, such as a zero-injection agreement, in place for the generator.
filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.quote: if the applicants are looking to co-locate the Load with the generation, then they will need to ensure that an appropriate Interconnection Agreement e.g. “ZGIA” has already been executed for the generator

filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.point: Paired generation can ask for up to 150 percent of the load's peak demand and must sit in the same resource zone.
filing-er27-526-miso-large-loads.quote: limits the requested interconnection service to 150 percent of the paired load’s peak demand, and requires the load and generation to be located in the same Local Resource Zone

filing-er27-527-miso-grits.point: GRITS is a permanent firm and non-firm contract demand service for large loads that can cut their withdrawals.
filing-er27-527-miso-grits.quote: GRITS provides a permanent firm and non-firm contract demand-based, Transmission Service option for Large Loads willing and able to limit their withdrawals under specified price and reliability conditions.

filing-er27-527-miso-grits.point: MISO says it answers FERC's concern that no permanent contract demand service exists in MISO.
filing-er27-527-miso-grits.quote: the need for a permanent contract demand transmission service in the MISO region

filing-er27-527-miso-grits.point: The earliest start is January 1, 2029, because of software changes.
filing-er27-527-miso-grits.quote: the earliest MISO will be able to implement GRITS is January 1, 2029

filing-er27-527-miso-grits.point: Example: a 500 MW load could take 200 MW firm and 300 MW non-firm.
filing-er27-527-miso-grits.quote: a Large Load Transmission Customer representing a Large Load of 500 MW may desire to only take 200 MW of firm transmission service

filing-er27-527-miso-grits.point: Customers need not move toward firm service.
filing-er27-527-miso-grits.quote: does not require the Large Load Transmission Customer to progress toward firm service for any or all of its GRITS Load Limit

filing-er27-527-miso-grits.point: GRITS is not limited to loads served by a co-located generator.
filing-er27-527-miso-grits.quote: is not limited to Large Load being served by a co-located generator

filing-er27-527-miso-grits.point: Rates are still being developed with the transmission owners.
filing-er27-527-miso-grits.quote: to continue the development of rates applicable to GRITS in concert with the MISO Transmission Owners

filing-er27-527-miso-grits.point: A customer must request GRITS through the Large Load Project Review, the same study route as other large-load service.
filing-er27-527-miso-grits.quote: A Large Load Transmission Customer must request GRITS through the applicable LLPR process
